documents.title: Microbiota-Bile acid decoupling contributes to altered postnatal growth and metabolism in sFGR: a twin-paired dynamic study with FMT validation.
documents.abstract: Selective fetal growth restriction (sFGR) increases the risk of adverse long-term metabolic outcomes, yet the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Bile acids (BAs) mediate gut microbiota-host metabolic crosstalk, and their early-life perturbation may underlie sFGR-associated health risks. Using a monochorionic diamniotic twin cohort (25 concordant pairs, 22 sFGR pairs), we developed a twin-specific analytical framework integrating birth weight deviation, intra-pair difference, and time-weighted variables. Through metagenomics, 16S rRNA sequencing, metabolomics, and fecal microbiota transplant

documents.title: Fecal microbiota transplantation in cancer immunotherapy: targeting the Gut-Tumor Axis.
documents.abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have transformed cancer therapy, but resistance and immune-related toxicities continue to limit their benefit. Fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) may enhance ICI efficacy and alleviate treatment-related intestinal toxicity, yet clinical responses remain inconsistent, and microbiome remodeling does not reliably predict benefit. Moreover, clinical, ecological, and mechanistic evidence remains fragmented and has not been critically integrated. This review therefore evaluates the current clinical evidence for FMT in cancer immunotherapy and examines how dono

documents.title: Lung microbiota in COPD: a double-edged sword.
documents.abstract: The respiratory microbiota constitutes a dynamic, low-biomass microbial ecosystem whose composition and function are shaped by continuous immigration, elimination, local growth conditions and host-environment interactions. Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) provides a clinically important model in which this ecological equilibrium is profoundly altered. This review examines the lung microbiota through a "double-edged sword" framework, proposing that its biological effects depend less on the presence of individual beneficial or pathogenic taxa than on community structure, ecological s

documents.title: Multiomics Approach to Regionally Profile Zinc-Driven Host-Gut Microbiome Interactions in the Intestinal Tract.
documents.abstract: Zinc (Zn) deficiency (ZnD) is a major risk factor for metabolic and inflammatory diseases associated with gut microbial alterations, including obesity, type 2 diabetes, and inflammatory bowel disease. Despite its importance, there are no established dietary recommendations for Zn supplementation in individuals with these conditions, except in cases of severe diarrhea in children. This gap stems from inconsistent outcomes in Zn supplementation trials, suggesting an incomplete understanding of Zn-mediated spatial regulation within the host-microbiome interface.
documents.journal: Cellular and molecular gastroenterology and hepatology

documents.title: The ecological impact of Ulva prolifera green tide outbreaks: microbial connectivity and metabolic divergence.
documents.abstract: Green tides in coastal areas have become an increasing eco-environmental concern around the world. However, the influence of massive green tides on microorganism dispersal has not yet been explored in detail. In this study, we used amplicon and metagenomic sequencing to first systematically examine the dynamics of the microbial community among continuous microhabitats in the Ulva prolifera bloom area. We found that the phycospheric microbiota exhibited increased α-diversity and complex network topologies. The tracking of bacterial sources indicated that phycospheric microorganisms originated f

documents.title: Complete coding sequence of a virus belonging to the Chaphamavirus genus identified in a pooled blood sample from Actitis macularius birds collected on the Brazilian Amazon coast.
documents.abstract: This study reports the identification of a virus belonging to the genus Chaphamavirus in Actitis macularius birds in Pará, Brazil. The genome exhibited significant genetic divergence compared to known sequences, highlighting the identification of a distinct genetic lineage and potentially prompting a future taxonomic reorganization within this viral group.

documents.title: Multi-scale hybrid correction of noisy long reads.
documents.abstract: Long-read sequencing offers superior genome resolution but is hindered by error rates of 1-15%. Existing correction methods often struggle to suppress sequencing errors without removing genuine biological variation, leading to over-correction. DADEC addresses this trade-off through a confidence-ordered framework comprising stringent de Bruijn graph (DBG) correction, haplotype-aware short-read alignment refinement, and permissive DBG recovery. Across seven simulated and three real datasets, DADEC achieved the lowest mismatch and indel rates in most benchmark settings while maintaining high hapl

documents.title: Global research trends in asthma during pregnancy: A multidisciplinary bibliometric analysis utilizing multiple databases (2008-2024).
documents.abstract: Asthma is a common chronic disease that poses a double threat to both pregnant women and the health of their fetuses. This study introduces the method of bibliometric analysis to systematically review the current research status of asthma during pregnancy worldwide, aiming to comprehensively analyze its knowledge structure, evolution trends, and emerging research frontiers.

documents.title: Sheep or cattle fecal contamination? Using long-read amplicon sequencing for fecal source attribution and apportionment.
documents.abstract: Fecal contamination of freshwater poses a risk to environmental and human health. Accurately attributing contamination to specific sources is critical for remediation. However, discriminating between closely related ruminants, sheep and cattle, remains a challenge. This study evaluated the use of fast expectation maximization microbial source tracking (FEAST) and mitochondrial and microbial source tracking (MST) qPCR markers for fecal source identification. The focus was differentiation between cattle and sheep sources using a spiked laboratory experiment with known fecal inputs and field test

documents.title: Genome-resolved multi-omics characterizes bacterial, viral, and metabolic components associated with Parkinson's disease gut ecosystem variation.
documents.abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is increasingly recognized as a disorder involving the gut-brain axis, yet genome-resolved characterization of bacterial and viral communities with metabolic context remains limited. Here, we performed deep shotgun metagenomic sequencing and fecal metabolomic profiling in a high-altitude cohort comprising patients with PD and environmentally matched spouse controls (living at approximately 1,900 m altitude). We reconstructed 455 species-level genome bins (SGBs) and 2,957 non-redundant viral operational taxonomic units (vOTUs), enabling high-resolution profiling of bact

documents.title: Urban avian viromes reveal viral diversity of potential public health relevance across China.
documents.abstract: Urbanization reshapes ecological interactions at the human-animal interface, yet how it structures viral diversity in urban avian communities remains unclear. Here, we present a pan-urban viromic analysis of avian samples collected across 22 cities in China. We identified 52,314 viral operational taxonomic units, broadly representing species-level viral clusters, revealing extensive and previously underexplored viral diversity. Viral richness varied markedly among cities, largely reflecting variation in bacteriophage diversity, whereas vertebrate-associated viruses showed a comparatively narro

documents.title: Aerobic and anaerobic cultivation shapes steroid-degrading wastewater consortia: Metagenomic insights into catabolic potential and antibiotic resistance genes.
documents.abstract: Steroid hormones such as 17β-estradiol (E2) and progesterone (P4) are emerging wastewater contaminants, yet the microbial communities and functional capabilities associated with their removal across different wastewater sources and cultivation conditions remain poorly understood. This study investigated P4- and E2-enriched consortia derived from dairy and municipal wastewater under aerobic and anaerobic cultivation conditions, integrating steroid degradation kinetics with shotgun metagenomic analysis. Aerobic consortia achieved >99% P4 removal within 9-12 h and E2 removal within 24 h, whereas

documents.title: Assessing dietary intake in infants through fecal sample analysis in the LLNEXT Cohort.
documents.abstract: Accurate diet tracing is fundamental to diet-health association studies, yet it remains challenging. This is particularly the case for early life studies, which rely on parental recall. Fecal sample analysis offers a non-invasive method for assessing those dietary components that have sufficient quantities of DNA remaining in stool, and are able to be taxonomically distinguished by marker gene sequence.
documents.journal: The American journal of clinical nutrition

documents.title: Diet Soda Consumption is Associated with Shifts in Gut Microbiome Function of Overweight Young Women.
documents.abstract: Low-calorie sweeteners (LCS) are consumed as sugar substitutes and may alter gut microbial composition. Their effects on microbial functional pathways and cardiometabolic physiology in humans remain poorly understood, particularly among individuals with overweight.
documents.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences

documents.title: Multi-omics signatures of growth and abdominal fat heterosis in Guangxi Sanhuang × Wenchang F1 chickens.
documents.abstract: Crossbreeding can combine complementary parental traits, but whether crosses between faster- and slower-growing yellow-feathered broilers balance growth and abdominal fat remains unclear. We compared contemporaneous purebred Guangxi Sanhuang (YY), F1 Guangxi Sanhuang sire × Wenchang dam (YX), and purebred Wenchang (XX) hens, estimating heterosis against purebred group means for this single cross direction. Duodenal RNA-seq, untargeted plasma metabolomics, and cecal metagenomics used eight hens per group. YX had intermediate week-15 body weight, average daily gain, and live, carcass, and evisce

documents.title: How to train your microbe: editing environmental bacteria.
documents.abstract: Genome editing is an essential tool in microbiology, enabling researchers to assess gene function, link genotype to phenotype, and design microbes with specific features. Most tools have been developed in model bacteria, and adapting them to environmental species remains time- and resource-intensive. This review provides a framework for engineering environmental bacteria, including assessment of genetic tractability, considerations for overcoming challenges in recalcitrant systems, and an overview of techniques with guidance on tool selection. We discuss the emerging field of microbiome editin

documents.title: The OMM12 model after ten years: what did we learn about the gut microbiome from a defined microbial community?
documents.abstract: Over the past decade, the Oligo-Mouse-Microbiota (OMM12) has emerged as a cornerstone model for mechanistic studies of the gut microbiome. As a rationally designed, defined microbial community, OMM12 reduces the complexity of the native microbiota while preserving key ecological and functional traits of the murine gut ecosystem. Comprising twelve culturable, genome-sequenced, and phenotypically characterized strains of murine origin, the model enables reproducible and stable colonization across hosts and experimental settings. Initially developed to study colonization resistance, OMM12 has sin

documents.title: Integrating Network Toxicology, Machine Learning, Gut Microbiome Analysis, and Structural Analysis to Reveal the Molecular Mechanisms Linking PFOA and PFOS Exposure to Age-Related Macular Degeneration.
documents.abstract: Perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA) and perfluorooctane sulfonic acid (PFOS) are persistent environmental contaminants with potential adverse effects on human health, but their involvement in age-related macular degeneration (AMD) remains poorly understood. Here, we integrated transcriptomics, network toxicology, machine learning, Mendelian randomization (MR), gut microbiome analysis, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulations to investigate potential molecular targets linking PFOA/PFOS exposure to AMD. A total of 97 potential PFOA/PFOS-AMD targets were identified, and integrative machine

documents.title: Broad-spectrum in situ genetic reprogramming of native microbiomes.
documents.abstract: Complex microbial communities are found throughout terrestrial, aquatic, and animal-associated ecosystems. Genetic modification of discrete microbial taxa within native communities represents a powerful tool to study and augment microbiome functions. Herein, we develop Synthetic Phage Assisted Reprogrammable and Targetable Addition (SPARTA) as a one-step strategy for packaging, delivering, and integrating large synthetic DNA into a broad range of native microbiomes. SPARTA leverages a broad-spectrum synthetic phage particle for in situ genome engineering within complex soil, freshwater, and ma
documents.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology

documents.title: NanoPAMDA enables rapid PAM characterization of metagenome-derived Cas9 effectors.
documents.abstract: CRISPR-Cas9 orthologs remain functionally underexplored despite the rapidly growing scale of publicly available metagenomic sequencing data. Here, we applied a multi-stage computational discovery pipeline to two independent sources of metagenomic sequence data, a multi-biome collection of 620,185 metagenome-assembled genomes spanning 17 public catalogs, and raw sequencing reads from human microbiome studies assembled de novo, to identify novel Cas9 orthologs. Candidates were filtered for guide RNA architectural plausibility, sequence novelty, conservation of catalytic residues, and structural
documents.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology

documents.title: Melon fruit microbiomes resemble aerial-tissue communities in a Turpan oasis field.
documents.abstract: Fruit-associated communities encounter belowground and aerial habitats, yet their position within the whole-plant microbiome remains unclear in field-grown melon. We profiled bacterial 16S rRNA gene and fungal internal transcribed spacer 1 (ITS1) amplicons from rhizosphere soil and surface-disinfected roots, stems, leaves and fruits. Four cultivars were sampled at fruit set and maturity in a randomised-block Turpan oasis field.

documents.title: Xuanfei Baidu Decoction and Its Active Component Glycyrrhizic Acid Ameliorate Insulin Resistance in Type 2 Diabetes via JNK/JAK/STAT Axis Inhibition.
documents.abstract: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is driven by insulin resistance and chronic inflammation, yet current single-target therapies inadequately address these interconnected pathologies. Xuanfei Baidu decoction (XFBD), originally developed for COVID-19, is known to inhibit JNK and JAK/STAT pathways and may offer a multi-target strategy.

documents.title: Artificial Intelligence for Colorectal Cancer Diagnosis: A Comprehensive Survey of Modalities, Frameworks, and Clinical Tasks.
documents.abstract: The diagnosis of colorectal cancer encompasses nine complementary modalities: stool-based screening, blood-based biomarkers, cross-sectional imaging, endoscopic evaluation, histopathology, liquid biopsy, molecular and genetic profiling, microbiome analysis, and nanotechnology-based diagnostics. This narrative review synthesizes 160 references spanning seven task-specific artificial intelligence domains, including computer-aided detection, optical diagnosis, invasion depth prediction, computational pathology and radiogenomics, metastasis forecasting, neoadjuvant treatment response prediction, a

documents.title: OmicsNCyc: An Integrated Pipeline for Fast Analysis of Nitrogen Cycle Functional Genes With a Curated Database.
documents.abstract: High-throughput sequencing has greatly advanced our understanding of microbial nitrogen (N) cycle gene families in various ecosystems. However, current workflows for profiling N cycling genes often require multiple analytical steps, and the complexity of parameters hampers inexperienced users. Here, we developed OmicsNCyc, a powerful tool for rapid, accurate, and scalable N cycling gene analysis. With a single command, OmicsNCyc offers users full-pipeline analysis from raw sequencing reads to statistical summaries and visualization, while also supporting specific analyses of individual N cycli

documents.title: Global biosynthetic potential of the phylum Acidobacteriota.
documents.abstract: Bacteria from the phylum Acidobacteriota are widely distributed across diverse environments yet only a few representatives have been isolated and described. Although recent studies suggest substantial biosynthetic potential in Acidobacteriota across soil and marine environments, no comprehensive cross-biome analysis of their biosynthetic diversity has been conducted. To address this gap, we analysed 19,720 metagenome-assembled genomes from Acidobacteriota along with their environmental description to provide a systematic overview of their biosynthetic potential. Our analyses reveal that Acidob

documents.title: Tradeoffs in Method Selection for Analyzing Full-Length 16S Data From Nanopore Sequencing in Defined and Environmental Microbiomes.
documents.abstract: Bacteria are found in nearly every environment on earth, and the ability to characterize bacterial communities is key to investigating a variety of scientific questions. One method for characterizing and comparing bacterial communities is to amplify and sequence the 16S ribosomal RNA gene and to use these sequences (A) to determine phylogenetic relationships within and between samples and (B) to assign a taxonomic identification to each sequence by comparison to reference databases. Nanopore sequencing technology has increased the accessibility and affordability of sequencing for full-length 1

documents.title: Taxonomic Guilds, Action Mechanisms, and Agronomic Deployment of Maize Rhizosphere Microbiota for Yield Enhancement: Unraveling G×M×E Interactions and Translational Barriers via Multi Omics.
documents.abstract: Maize (Zea mays L.) productivity is increasingly constrained by edaphic stressors-including soil salinization, drought, and acidification-posing mounting threats to global food security. Plant growth-promoting microorganisms (PGPM) offer a sustainable alternative to synthetic fertilizers, yet despite their pronounced performance under controlled laboratory settings, their beneficial effects often prove inconsistent in open-field environments, largely due to spatial heterogeneity and genotype-specific responses. Herein, we present a comprehensive synthesis of the core microbial guilds that have

documents.title: Gut microbial metabolite indole-3-lactic acid may bind to IL1B: An in silico network pharmacology study of the gut-pulmonary artery axis in pulmonary arterial hypertension.
documents.abstract: ObjectivePulmonary arterial hypertension is a progressive pulmonary vascular disease in which inflammation contributes to vascular remodeling. Pulmonary arterial hypertension has been linked to gut microbiota dysbiosis, but the specific metabolite-target interactions remain unclear. This study aimed to computationally identify key gut microbial metabolites and their molecular targets in pulmonary arterial hypertension regulation using an in silico network pharmacology approach.MethodsThis in silico network pharmacology study was neither retrospective nor prospective because no human participan
documents.journal: The Journal of international medical research

documents.title: A Multilevel Perspective on the Skin: Skin Architecture, Microbial Communities, Intrinsic Metabolites, and Emerging AI-Enabled Applications.
documents.abstract: The skin is the largest organ of the human body and harbors a diverse microbial community that constitutes a complex ecosystem. Despite advances in next-generation sequencing (NGS) that have greatly facilitated the characterization of skin microbiota composition, a critical gap remains in understanding how intrinsic metabolites mediate host-microbe interactions and maintain microecological homeostasis. This review synthesizes current knowledge across interconnected layers of the skin ecosystem, including architecture, microbial communities, metabolites, and computational analytics. The skin's

documents.title: Global Analysis of Public Cheese Microbiomes Reveals Widespread Bacterial Taxa and Geographic Community Structure.
documents.abstract: Cheese microbiomes remain difficult to compare globally because public sequencing datasets are fragmented and methodologically heterogeneous. Here, we curated 14,203 sequencing records from 233 BioProjects and retained 8910 records from 112 BioProjects for standardized reanalysis, establishing a global comparative framework for cheese microbiome research. Three taxonomic profiling pipelines (QIIME2, Kraken2 and mOTUs) recovered broadly consistent genus-level patterns dominated by lactic acid bacteria, although quantitative concordance varied between methods and study collections. Whole-genome

documents.title: Next-Generation Sequencing Reveals the Total Yeast and Mold Species Present in Greenhouse-Grown Cannabis Inflorescences-Implications for Quality Control.
documents.abstract: Next-generation sequencing (NGS) was conducted to determine the composition of the fungal and yeast species (mycobiome) within inflorescences of seven THC-containing genotypes of cannabis (Cannabis sativa L.). They were grown under conventional hydroponic cultivation or under organic production in commercial greenhouses. Up to 26 fungal and yeast species were identified from DNA sequence homologies to representative species in databanks. The mycobiome composition varied according to cultivation method, cannabis genotype, and post-harvest drying. Highest numbers of total fungal reads were prese

documents.title: The Impact of Intratumoral Bacterial Response to Vaccine Therapy in Cancer Treatment.
documents.abstract: Therapeutic Human papillomavirus (HPVs) vaccines are designed to enhance the immunogenicity of HPV and promote the elimination of tumor cells effectively. Mounting evidence implies that tumor-resident microbiomes may influence therapeutic outcomes through immune modulation. In this study, we evaluated whether the intratumoral microbiota affects the efficacy of the therapeutic HPV vaccine. We analyzed RNA sequencing data from tumor tissues of C57BL/6N female mice treated with a DNA vaccine incorporating HPV16 E6/E7 antigens fused with the chemokine CCL11. Microbial community data were acquired

documents.title: Active temperate phages linked to core bacterial taxa dominate the wheat phyllosphere virome.
documents.abstract: The wheat phyllosphere supports diverse microbial communities, yet the viral life-history strategies that enable persistence in this dynamic habitat remain largely unknown. Accordingly, 36 non-amplified double-stranded DNA viromes were analyzed across tissues, years, and continents to test whether temperate phages are the dominant component of the wheat phyllosphere virome. A total of 7958 viral operational taxonomic units (vOTUs) were identified, including 1211 high-quality or complete genomes, revealing extensive viral novelty. Among 726 active vOTUs, the virome was structured around a persi

documents.title: Ginseng-Douchi ameliorates high-fat diet-induced obesity and metabolic disorders via gut microbiota regulation.
documents.abstract: This study evaluated the anti-obesity effects of Ginseng-Douchi (SC), a novel functional food fermented from ginseng and soybean (both medicinal and edible resources) using Bacillus subtilis, and explored its gut microbiota regulatory mechanisms in high-fat diet (HFD)-induced obese mice.

documents.title: Genomic resilience of aquatic microbes in Sangam: insights from the Mahakumbh event.
documents.abstract: The Mahakumbh festival at Prayagraj represents an exceptionally intense and temporally concentrated anthropogenic perturbation superimposed on the dynamic riverine ecosystem at the confluence of the Ganga and Yamuna rivers. The large gathering of people during the festival can alter organic loading, nutrient availability, turbidity, dissolved oxygen, microbial inputs, and exposure to pharmaceutical, fecal, and other anthropogenic contaminants, thereby providing a valuable natural observational framework for investigating microbial community responses to environmental disturbance. This review s

documents.title: Decoding the functional differentiation of herb pairs in Tong-Xie-Yao-Fang: effects on gut microbiota, intestinal barrier function, and Wnt signaling in IBS-D mice.
documents.abstract: Diarrhea-predominant irritable bowel syndrome (IBS-D) is a prevalent functional gastrointestinal disorder with limited therapeutic options. Tong-Xie-Yao-Fang (TXYF), a classical Chinese herbal formula, has shown clinical efficacy, but the respective contributions of its full formula and of its constituent herb pairs, "Tonifying Tu (Earth)" (TT) and "Suppressing Mu (Wood)" (SM), remain incompletely characterized, particularly with respect to the interplay among the gut microbiota, the intestinal barrier, and Wnt signaling.

documents.title: Bifidobacterium supplementation preserves gut microbiota stability and enhances wellbeing during short-term international travel: a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial.
documents.abstract: Short-term international travel represents an acute environmental perturbation that can disrupt the gut microbiome and contribute to gastrointestinal, respiratory, and psychological symptoms. Probiotic supplementation has been proposed as a strategy to enhance microbiome resilience; however, its effects on both microbial dynamics and multi-domain health outcomes during travel remain incompletely understood.

documents.title: Dysbiosis of the commensal microbiota in IgA nephropathy.
documents.abstract: Immunoglobulin A nephropathy (IgAN) is a common form of primary glomerulonephritis. Its pathophysiology remains unclear, and no curative treatment has yet been developed. Although abnormal mucosal immune responses to exogenous antigens have been implicated in the onset and progression of IgAN, the mucosal sites responsible for these responses may differ between Asian and Western populations. Furthermore, previous studies investigating the commensal microbiota on mucosal surfaces have identified multiple bacterial taxa that are significantly associated with IgAN; however, few bacterial species

documents.title: A mosaic of bacterial communities and their functional potential across Antarctic moss, lichen and soil.
documents.abstract: Bacterial community composition differed markedly among substrates, whereas broad community-level differences between sampling localities were not statistically detected. The recovered U. aurantiacoatra bacterial community was dominated by Pseudomonadota, while A. regularis and soil communities exhibited greater taxonomic diversity, with Pseudomonadota, Actinomycetota, and Cyanobacteriota as dominant phyla. Functional profiling revealed distinct metabolic patterns across microhabitats. Bulk soils exhibited the broadest metabolic potential and nearly complete nitrogen-cycling pathways. The A. r

documents.title: Population structure and sampling shape genomic antimicrobial resistance patterns in 30,327 Clostridioides difficile genomes.
documents.abstract: Background. Large collections of publicly available bacterial genomes can be used to examine antimicrobial resistance (AMR), but estimates from such collections may be influenced by over-representation of particular lineages and by the method used to identify resistance markers. These effects were examined in a large collection of Clostridioides difficile genomes. Methods. All C. difficile GenBank assemblies available on 20 August 2026 were identified. After exclusion of records flagged by the National Center for Biotechnology Information (NCBI) as atypical or metagenome-assembled, application

documents.title: Comparative shotgun metagenomic analysis of the feline fecal microbiome in response to fresh, dry, and wet diets in a randomized crossover trial.
documents.abstract: Fresh (mildly cooked) cat foods are an increasingly popular alternative to conventional extruded dry and retorted wet diets, differing in their processing and formulation. While the gut microbiota play an important role in feline health and physiological functions, characterization of the gut microbiome in cats fed fresh diets and direct comparisons with dry and wet diets have not yet been performed. In this 42-day, 3 × 3 Latin square crossover trial, 15 healthy adult cats received commercial, chicken-based, complete fresh, dry, and wet diets in one of three randomized diet sequences. Each die

documents.title: Microbial community structure and functional gene profiles of drinking water treatment plant sludge in South Africa: An exploratory pilot study.
documents.abstract: Microbial characterization of drinking water treatment plant (DWTP) sludge helps inform sludge management strategies and supports the development of disposal policies and procedures. In South Africa, the microbial composition of DWTP sludge remains poorly documented. This study characterised the microbial communities and functional gene profiles in sludge samples collected from three DWTPs in Gauteng, Limpopo, and Mpumalanga. A shotgun metagenomic approach was employed to provide a broad assessment of microbial taxa and functional gene categories, while physicochemical analyses were conducted

documents.title: The bumble bee gut microbiota: ecological dynamics, functional roles and environmental responses.
documents.abstract: Bumble bees (Bombus spp.) are important pollinators in natural and agricultural ecosystems, but many species are increasingly exposed to interacting pressures including habitat alteration, climate change, pesticides, nutritional stress, and pathogens. The gut microbiota has emerged as a potentially important component of bumble bee biology, with evidence linking host-associated microorganisms to nutrition, immunity, and pathogen resistance. Bumble bees harbor a relatively simple and specialized gut community dominated by recurrent bacterial lineages including Snodgrassella, Gilliamella, Bombis

documents.title: Effects of a multistrain probiotic formulation on immune response and microbiome modulation following influenza vaccination in adults: a randomised, triple-blind, placebo-controlled trial.
documents.abstract: Seasonal influenza remains a major global health burden, despite widespread vaccination. Vaccine responsiveness varies considerably between individuals and is increasingly recognised to be influenced by host factors, including the gut microbiome. Probiotics have been proposed as a strategy to modulate microbiome-immune interactions, although their effects on vaccine responses and the underlying microbial mechanisms remain incompletely understood.

documents.title: Genome skimming of Poecilosclerida (Porifera) reveals conserved and hyperrearranged mitochondrial genomes.
documents.abstract: Genome skimming is a cost-effective approach that efficiently recovers multi-copy genomic regions, making it particularly valuable for phylogenetic research and biodiversity assessments. In this study, we applied shallow shotgun metagenome sequencing to 15 poecilosclerid sponges, successfully assembling complete mitochondrial genomes for four species and full rDNA clusters for the majority of samples, despite considerable variation in the retrieval of genomic regions and exogenous, non-poriferan sequences. Phylogenetic reconstructions using both rDNA and mtDNA sequences uncovered extensive pol

documents.title: Exploratory randomized trial of the bacterial lysate Qipian in stable COPD: peripheral inflammatory, gut and airway microbiota, and fecal metabolomic changes.
documents.abstract: To explore Qipian-associated changes in clinical symptoms, systemic inflammation, microbiota, and metabolomic profiles in patients with stable chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD).

documents.title: Effects of long-term exposure to four widely used drinking water regimens on growth performance and fecal microbiota in C57BL/6J mice.
documents.abstract: Gut microbiota plays a vital role in regulating host physiological status and is susceptible to environmental factors, including different drinking water regimens. This study aimed to explore the effects of long-term exposure to four commonly used drinking water regimens on growth performance and fecal microbiota in C57BL/6J mice. A total of 32 male mice were randomly divided into four groups and continuously administered reverse osmosis water (ROW), hydrochloric acid-acidified water (HCl-AW), sulfuric acid-acidified water (H2SO4-AW), and chlorinated water (CW) for 12 weeks, respectively. Body

documents.title: Elsholtzia Bodinieri vaniot dichloromethane extract exerts anti-inflammatory effects in acute lung injury mice by regulating the CCR1 and FLT1.
documents.abstract: Acute lung injury (ALI) is a disease characterized by diffuse dysfunction leading to systemic inflammation, increased vascular permeability and loss of alveolar epithelial cell function. Elsholtzia bodinieri Vaniot is a traditional folk medicinal and edible plant endowed with heat-clearing(Qingre) and detoxifying efficacies.

documents.title: Analysis of the biological characteristics and gene function of Lactobacillus delbrueckii subsp. sunkii.
documents.abstract: The biological characteristics, morphology, and genomic information of Lactobacillus delbrueckii subsp. sunkii, isolated from the vaginal secretions of pregnant women, have not yet been reported. Elucidating its biological properties and genetic functions may provide a theoretical foundation for developing probiotic preparations to treat bacterial vaginosis. The strain was identified as L. delbrueckii subsp. sunkii using mass spectrometry and 16S ribosomal RNA (16S rRNA) gene sequencing. Colony morphology was observed, Gram staining characteristics were examined, and cellular ultrastructure wa

documents.title: Association of in utero and postnatal drought exposure with health and anthropometric outcomes in children under-five: A systematic review.
documents.abstract: Drought poses multiple health risks that may affect children both prenatally and during early childhood, yet the evidence remains fragmented. We conducted a systematic review to synthesize evidence from observational studies assessing the association between drought exposure during pregnancy and the first five years of life and child health and anthropometric outcomes. The review protocol was registered in PROSPERO (CRD4202338273). We searched 18 databases and complemented the search with grey literature and manual reference screening. Two independent reviewers screened studies and assessed ri

documents.title: Microbiome variation across the intestinal dysbiosis landscape is linked to inflammation and transit time.
documents.abstract: Intestinal dysbiosis, an imbalance in gut microbial composition and host-microbiome interaction, has been linked to various conditions and disorders. Although characterised by multiple features, such as reduced microbial diversity and bacterial load, as well as an underrepresentation of beneficial microorganisms and an overrepresentation of pathobionts, an exact definition remains elusive. Whether all dysbiotic individuals share similar microbial composition and host properties is currently unclear.

documents.title: The rising burden of chronic gastrointestinal diseases: the role of Mediterranean diet.
documents.abstract: Chronic gastrointestinal (GI) and metabolic diseases represent a growing global healthcare burden, heavily influenced by environmental factors and the exposome. This comprehensive review evaluates the therapeutic and preventative role of the Mediterranean diet (MD) as a potent non-pharmacological intervention in modulating gut health. A literature analysis was conducted focusing on the mechanisms of the MD-rich in polyphenols, monounsaturated fatty acids, and dietary fiber-and its clinical impact on pediatric Inflammatory Bowel Disease (IBD), gluten-related disorders, functional GI disorders,

documents.title: From conventional monitoring to agentic AI: integration of data streams and computational tools for real-time microalgal surveillance.
documents.abstract: Microalgal cultivation generates continuous and diverse data streams, including physicochemical sensor measurements, optical and spectroscopic signals, and episodic molecular tests. Together, these data characterize cultivation conditions at different biological scales. Existing AI/ML frameworks can interpret these streams independently; however, human intervention is required to translate predictions into cultivation decisions, adding delays and limiting adaptability across strains, reactors, and environmental conditions. This mini-review describes the transition from conventional monitoring

documents.title: Potential for Improvement in the Metabolic Profiles of Patients With Hepatic Steatosis After Behavioral Change Associated With the Use of Probiotics or Vitamin E.
documents.abstract: This study aimed to evaluate the effects of changing eating habits and regular physical exercise, alone or in combination with vitamin E or probiotic supplementation, on the clinical and biochemical profiles, body composition, and gut microbiota of adult male patients diagnosed with hepatic steatosis.

documents.title: Prolong Life with Nine Turn-Method versus CBT-I for Sleep-Onset Chronic Insomnia: A Randomized Controlled Trial Protocol Integrating fMRI and PSG.
documents.abstract: Sleep-onset chronic insomnia is one of the most common sleep disorders in clinical practice and carries a substantial multidimensional burden, including somatic symptoms, emotional distress, and impaired quality of life. Although Prolong Life with Nine Turn-Method has long been used to promote sleep, its specific efficacy for this subtype lacks adequate empirical support.

documents.title: Metadoon: A user-friendly GUI for amplicon analysis.
documents.abstract: The analysis of microbial communities through 16S rRNA gene sequencing plays a central role in microbial ecology and host-associated microbiome research. However, the complexity of existing bioinformatic tools often limits their use by researchers without computational expertise. We present Metadoon, a graphical pipeline designed to automate the analysis of amplicon sequencing data targeting the V3-V4 regions of the 16S rRNA gene. Developed in Python and integrating VSEARCH and R, Metadoon performs quality filtering, OTU clustering, taxonomic classification, and diversity analysis through an i

documents.title: Species-specific gut microbiome responses to rodenticide exposure: restructuring in greenfinches but stability in pigeons.
documents.abstract: Rodent eradication on oceanic islands is essential for the conservation of endemic species. Although anticoagulant rodenticides (ARs) are widely used for rodent control, their potential impacts on non-target wildlife require careful evaluation. We focused on the gut microbiome as a non-invasive indicator of AR exposure. Here, we administered ARs to Oriental greenfinches (Chloris sinica minor) and rock dove (Columba livia) as surrogate species for the critically endangered Bonin greenfinch (Chloris kittlitzi) and red-headed wood pigeon (Columba janthina nitens) to evaluate gut microbiome respon

documents.title: Towards symbiont-based visceral leishmaniosis control: Delftia tsuruhatensis TC1 shows anti- Leishmania infantum effect in Phlebotomus perniciosus.
documents.abstract: Visceral leishmaniosis caused by Leishmania infantum is a grave disease solely transmitted by vector sand flies with a high risk of mortality when left untreated. The introduction of symbiont bacteria with anti-parasitic properties within vector species represents a promising biological control strategy for vector-borne diseases. In this context, the symbiont bacterium Delftia tsuruhatensis strain TC1 (TC1) has previously demonstrated an in vivo antiparasitic effect in the sand fly Phlebotomus duboscqi against Leishmania major, the causative agent of cutaneous leishmaniosis.
